transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ____. Well, the main reason I came in is that I just get pulled off track so easily. It's like... if I'm working on a school project, say, a dashboard I'm supposed to be finishing for a class, and I get one Slack ping, or I hear a song lyric, or even just get a random idea for something completely different, suddenly I’ve completely lost the thread of what I was doing. It just happens all the time.
Do you also lose focus when you're doing things you actually enjoy?

Yeah, it actually does. Like, I can sit down to read a research article or watch a UX tutorial that I'm genuinely interested in for my major, but after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes have just been moving across the page or the screen, and I have absolutely no idea what I just took in. I end up having to rewind or reread the whole thing.
Do you often feel physically restless, like you need to fidget, squirm, or get up when you’re supposed to stay seated?

Yeah, definitely. Um, like in group meetings or portfolio reviews for my classes, I'm almost always bouncing my leg. Or clicking my pen, twisting my rings around... I just end up shifting around in my chair a lot. I honestly don't really notice I'm doing it until someone looks at me and I realize I've been moving the whole time.
Did these attention and restlessness symptoms start when you were a child?

Yeah, they did. Even back in elementary school, I remember my teachers would write comments on my report cards about how I'd rush through worksheets or just completely lose track of the directions. And they'd always mention that I talked over my classmates during group work. My parents actually had to sit right next to me while I did my homework, because if they didn't, I'd just wander off or start doing something else before I finished. So, yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
Do you often act before thinking, like interrupting people or blurting things out?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially when people are brainstorming for a project. I'll just blurt out my idea, or I'll even start adding things to their Figma board before they've finished explaining what they're thinking. I just get really excited in the moment, but I can tell afterward that I probably came off as pushy, even though I didn't mean to.
